topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and introduces its learning objectives.

topics.label: Mutations, clonal evolution and cancer susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations can give rise to cancer through clonal evolution and why susceptibility to that process varies.

topics.label: Environmental influences on cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how strongly environmental exposures contribute to cancer risk rather than cancer being solely inherited or a matter of chance.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of interacting infectious causes.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage by environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental carcinogens produce molecular damage that can become mutations in DNA.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why initiating mutations may require a growth-promoting environment before tumours develop.

topics.label: Context-dependent susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on the exposed tissue's biological context and consolidate the preceding account of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Identifying and assessing carcinogenic exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and methodological limitations involved in determining whether an exposure is carcinogenic.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This closing draws together the lecture's conclusions and places them in the context of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
